newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Escondida says no comment on strike, output.
newsitem.headline: Chile Escondida says no comment on strike, output.

text.p: The chief executive officer of Chile's giant Escondida copper mine, Ken Pickering Thursday declined to comment on statements by unions that the mine had run out of concentrates.
"I'm sorry but he won't make any comment," an Escondida spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.
Pickering said Wednesday that concentrate production and shipments were normal.
Union president Hugo Fernandez earlier told Reuters that mine output had been paralyzed by the week-old strike and a go-slow by non-unionized workers.
"We can tell you there are four or five ships in the port of Coloso at this moment but there is no concentrate. The mine doesn't have any more concentrate," Fernandez said.

Workers voted 131 to 127 to accept the company wage offer Wednesday night, but the 100-odd strikers who did not vote were counted as supporting the strike, which began last Friday after scheduled wage talks failed.
The Escondida union's 358 workers began striking last Friday, but 2,000 non-unionized workmates stayed on the job.
Fernandez said that communications with the company had completely broken down.

The workers are calling for better productivity bonuses, compensation for wages lost during the strike and a five percent pay rise for each year of the two-year collective labor contract. Escondida is offering no pay rise, he said.
The 800,000-tonne-a-year mine is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ-CRA.
